messages:
mia: thinking out loud — the rerank payload is getting huge for our large candidate sets. proposing a "compact-v1" score format: quantized 16-bit ints + base64 blob + a small header. would cut network by ~6x for 100 candidates. thoughts?
eric: love the idea. protobuf would also help (binary + schemas). have we bench'd decode cost on mobile clients?
jon: big +1 on size, but SDKs will break if we change shape. we need a negotiation path (Accept header or ?score_format=). also consider gradual rollout flags in console.
sara: can we server-side translate? i.e., let endpoint accept compact and always expose floats to older SDKs behind a compatibility flag. that keeps client change minimal.
mia: yes — my thought: default stays legacy JSON floats. add `X-Score-Format: compact-v1` response header when we serve compact. client opt-in via header `Accept-Score: compact-v1` or `?score_format=compact-v1`. server keeps `X-Score-Format` for telemetry/consumers.
kai: routing/model selection question: if compact -> likely using q8/q16 kernel or different model variant. should that affect routing policies? e.g., prefer cheaper cluster if client requested compact?
eric: routing needs to be explicit. compact is just a wire format; quantization/variant is an orthogonal knob. but we should expose `X-Model-Variant: redwood-7b-q16` and `X-Serving-Quant: q16` so operators and consumers can reason about it.
jon: console rollout UX: per-route toggle for `enable_compact_scores` + rollout percentage. also a global fallback that rewrites to legacy for routes with `compatibility=true`. we should add clear warning in the UI that compact responses may be lossy.
sara: telemetry: track `score_format`, `served_variant`, `decode_ms`, `payload_bytes` per request. we'll add them to our existing per-route trace. also patch alerts if `decode_ms` spikes.
mia: example compact response prototype:
```json
{"fmt":"q16","n":5,"blob":"AABBAA...base64...","meta":"min=-1,max=1"}
```
mia: server would also support `translate=true` query that returns decoded floats even if stored compact internally (for SDK compatibility during rollout).
jon: how do we account for quota units? currently 1 candidate = 1 score unit. compact shouldn't change billing. but we need clear docs: billing counts logical candidate-scoring ops, not bytes.
kai: agree. but note: if compact enables higher batch sizes / cheaper model variants, effective cost per logical op will drop — fine but billing should stay consistent. ops-team: flag if clients start abusing compact to squeeze throughput limits.
ops-bot: note created: #ticket-INC-4821 created for "compact score format telemetry". assigned to @sara.
deploy-bot: canary deploy of "compact-score-proto v1" started in eu-west-1.
eric: security: ensure base64 blobs are validated for length and we have strict schema. no arbitrary nested data. also add `schema_version` field.
sara: action items: 1) RFC draft for compact-v1 (mia) 2) Bench decode perf on iOS/Android (eric) 3) Console toggle + rollout UI (jon) 4) Telemetry fields & alert (sara) 5) Quota docs update (billing) 6) Server-side translate endpoint (mia/sara). i'll own telemetry ticket.
mia: i'll drop the RFC in the docs repo by EOD.
eric: quick perf note — CPU decode seems fine for q16; q8 decode needs SIMD path optimization on mobile. add to bench.
jon: SDK owners — plan a minor bump that reads `X-Score-Format` and handles compact if present, otherwise fallback. deprecate legacy shape after 3 months of rollout.
mia: thanks all. tagging this for follow-up in eng-platform sync.
